q)), \"the extremal graphs are complete bipartite graphs minus the edges of a star, plus isolated vertices.\"\n\nRegarding your specific questions:\n- **q=4**: The abstract doesn't isolate results {"parentUuid":"862c4fcc-0701-4051-b4ee-54f6546540e0","isSidechain":true,"agentId":"adac8bb48345a125f","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5","id":"msg_011CeH23L6qVRntZNdPR4NwG","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"# M2 — The Cap half of the Coloring-Mass Law: routes, literature, and a proof skeleton\n\nMethod note: the session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200), so the survey was done via direct WebFetch of arXiv/ar5iv/API URLs ([FV] = fetched and verified this session; [KB] = from background knowledge, not independently verifiable online this session; Semantic Scholar API was 429-throttled throughout). All empirical claims below were computed fresh from `results/theorem/fr_table/configs_r*.jsonl` + `data/d1_corpus.jsonl`.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Route 1 — Tait correspondence for disks: this is an exact identity, and I verified it on your data\n\n**Exact statement (disk version).** Let S be a near-triangulation of the disk (simple plane graph, outer face bounded by a cycle, every internal face a triangle) with n vertices. Identify the 3 edge-colors with the nonzero elements of the Klein group Z2×Z2. Then:\n\n- **Forward:** every proper 4-coloring c : V(S) → Z2×Z2 induces the edge labeling e = uv ↦ c(u)+c(v); labels are nonzero (properness) and the three labels on any triangle are pairwise distinct (equal labels on two edges of a triangle would force equal endpoint colors). So it is a triangle-distinct edge 3-coloring (\"tri-coloring\") of **all** edges of S.\n- **Backward (this is where the disk matters):** a tri-coloring is a Z2×Z2-valued 1-cochain whose sum around every internal face is 0 (three distinct nonzero Klein elements sum to 0). In a disk the internal face boundaries generate the whole cycle space, so the cochain is exact: it integrates to a vertex 4-coloring, unique up to the 4 global translations. **No cubic/bridgeless hypothesis is needed** — simple-connectivity replaces it. (For a closed triangulation of the sphere this is the classical Tait/Heawood equivalence in Klein-group form; the disk version is folklore/standard [KB] — e.g. it is exactly RSST's own remark that tri-colorings of the free completion correspond to 4-colorings; I found no single canonical reference stating the disk version with the counting constant, so it should be proved inline in the write-up. The proof is the 6-line cohomology argument above.)\n\n**Counting constants (all verified):**\n- #tri-colorings(S) = P(S,4)/4.\n- The S3 recoloring action on tri-colorings is **free**: a tri-coloring fixed by a transposition could use only the fixed color (kills triangles); one fixed by a 3-cycle would have no fixed edge label at all. Hence #(tri-colorings up to color symmetry) = **P(S,4)/24 exactly**.\n- Color-equivalent tri-colorings restrict to color-equivalent ring colorings, and distinct elements of Φ pull back to disjoint orbit sets, so\n\n  **Bridge Lemma: a = |Φ(K)| ≤ P(S,4)/24,** with equality iff no two color-inequivalent tri-colorings share a ring restriction.\n\n**Computational verification on the repo's own graphs** (brute-force P(G,4) on the stored adjacencies): `fr-r8-n9-0` (wheel, k=1): a = 43 = P/24 exactly; `fr-r10-n11-0`: a = 171 = P/24 exactly; `fr-r8-n12-120`: a = 81 ≤ P/24 = 92; `fr-r8-n12-164`: a = 77 ≤ P/24 = 85. Moreover the closed wheel formula P(W_r,4) = 4·(2^r+2) gives (2^r+2)/6, matching the observed max-a at k=1 for **every** even r in the table (43, 171, 683 at r = 8, 10, 12; odd r off by the predicted fixed-point rounding: 85 vs 85.67). So the stored `n_extendable` is exactly the |Φ| of this identity, and the identity is the correct bridge: **the Cap is now a pure chromatic-polynomial extremal problem** — maximize P(T,4) over triangulated disks with boundary length r, k interior vertices, interior degrees ≥5.\n\n---\n\n## 2. The theorem you can prove today: shelling gives B(r,k) = 2^(r+k−3), i.e. γ = 2\n\n**Lemma (shellability).** Every triangulated 2-ball is shellable — classical, dimension 2 only (attributed to Newman 1926; see also Danaraj–Klee's survey) [KB — this citation needs pinning down in the write-up, but the fact is uncontroversial; non-shellable balls first appear in dimension 3]. In a shelling, each added triangle meets the current complex in one or two full edges (edge + isolated vertex is not a legal shelling step). Consequence: there is a build order starting from one triangle in which **every new vertex arrives adjacent to the two endpoints of an existing edge**, so at q = 4 it has ≤ 2 available colors.\n\n**Theorem (Cap, γ=2).** For any near-triangulation S of the disk with n = r + k vertices: P(S,4) ≤ 4·3·2·2^(n−3) = 24·2^(n−3), hence by the Bridge Lemma\n\n  **a ≤ B(r,k) = 2^(r+k−3) = 2^(r−3)·2^k.**\n\nB is increasing in k, explicit, and — important negative check — **needs no interior-degree hypothesis at all**; min-degree 5 is purely a resource for improving γ (Section 5). Tightness: at k = 1 the bound is 2^(r−2) vs. the true wheel value 2^r/6 — within a factor 1.5. Against all 100k+ data cells the bound holds with huge slack at large k (true per-k growth ≈ 1.2 vs 2).\n\n**Gap flags for this theorem:** (i) pin the shelling citation and write the 1-page proof that shelling steps have the two combinatorial types claimed; (ii) confirm the stored graphs are the free completions (they are: ring = induced outer cycle, vertices 1..r, all internal faces triangles — checked on samples); (iii) the S3-freeness lemma (proved above, trivial). Nothing else. **This is a complete, low-risk proof.** As far as I can find, even this bound is unrecorded in the literature for this extremal class (see §3–4), so M2 at γ=2 is both provable now and publishable as part of the note.\n\n**Corollary arithmetic (why γ matters).** With Threshold A(r) ≥ α·2.4^r (M3, conjectural) and Cap a ≤ 2^(r−3)·γ^k, D-reducibility forces k·log2 γ ≥ r·log2(2.4/2) + O(1), i.e. **f(r) ≥ (0.263/log2 γ)·r − O(1)**:\n| γ | implied slope f(r)/r | status |\n|---|---|---|\n| 2 | 0.263 | **provable now** (shelling) |\n| 1.618 (φ) | 0.379 | Shrock–Tsai lattice bound, transplant needed |\n| 1.461 (Baxter bulk) | 0.480 | bulk entropy, not a bound for disks |\n| 4/3 | 0.634 | empirically sharp (see §5) |\n\nObserved truth: f(12)/12 ≈ 0.583. So even γ=2 already converts the finite table into an **infinite-r linear lower bound** f(r) ≳ 0.26r (conditional on T), and γ = 4/3 would essentially *recover the true growth rate of f(r)* — strong evidence the mass law is the right mechanism, not just an inequality.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Route 2 — chromatic-polynomial bounds and transfer matrices: what the literature actually has\n\n- **Birkhoff–Lewis 1946** (\"Chromatic polynomials\", Trans. AMS) [KB]: develops exactly the \"free vs. constrained polynomials of a triangulation with a ring\" formalism for rings 3–5 (partially 6) and *lower* bounds P(T,q) ≥ q(q−1)(q−2)(q−3)^(n−3) for q ≥ 5; the q=4 statements remain the \"Birkhoff–Lewis unsolved problems\". Their linear relations among ring-constrained polynomials are the ancestral form of your transfer-matrix structure, but they give **no upper bounds**. (arXiv has nothing under \"Birkhoff–Lewis\" except Hamiltonian-dynamics namesakes — [FV] http://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all:%22Birkhoff-Lewis%22.)\n- **Tutte's chromatic sums** (1973 series, Canad. J. Math.) [KB]: exact generating functions for Σ P(T,q) *averaged* over rooted planar triangulations, plus the golden identity P(T, φ+2) = (φ+2)·φ^(3n−10)·P(T, φ+1)² — beautiful at q = φ+2 ≈ 3.618 but silent at q = 4; averages don't cap the max.\n- **Transfer matrices, the directly relevant machinery** — Jacobsen–Salas–Sokal, \"Transfer Matrices and Partition-Function Zeros for Antiferromagnetic Potts Models III: Triangular-Lattice Chromatic Polynomial\", J. Stat. Phys. 112 (2003) 921–1017 [FV] https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0204587 (also IV, cyclic b.c., cond-mat/0407444 [FV via listing]). They compute chromatic polynomials of width-m triangular strips (m ≤ 12) via Fortuin–Kasteleyn/Temperley–Lieb transfer matrices whose state space is indexed by **non-crossing partitions of the ring** — precisely the \"fixed r, add a layer = linear map\" structure you flagged. This machinery *reconstructs Baxter's thermodynamic-limit curve*, confirming that for **layered** interiors the per-layer operator norm is governed by Baxter's W.\n- **Baxter's exact bulk entropy** [KB: Baxter, J. Phys. A 19 (1986) 2821 & 20 (1987) 5241, triangular-lattice chromatic polynomial]: per-site number of 4-colorings of the triangular lattice **W(tri,4) ≈ 1.4610**. Cross-confirmed numerically this session via Shrock–Tsai's ratio table (below): 1.333/0.913 = 1.460 = 1.618/1.107. The q=4 triangular AF Potts ground-state ensemble has a height representation and is critical (Moore–Newman 1999 [FV via listing] arXiv:cond-mat/9902295) — meaning no exponential decay of boundary influence at q=4, so *Dobrushin-style* uniqueness arguments are unavailable (Salas–Sokal cond-mat/9603068 [FV via listing] need q ≥ 11 on the triangular lattice).\n- **Rigorous per-site upper bound** — Shrock–Tsai, \"Upper and Lower Bounds for Ground State Entropy of Antiferromagnetic Potts Models\" (Phys. Rev. E 55 (1997)) [FV] https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/cond-mat/9701162 : for the triangular lattice, (q−2)²/(q−1) ≤ W ≤ ½[q−3+√(q²−6q+13)]; **at q = 4 the rigorous upper bound is the golden ratio φ ≈ 1.618** (lower 4/3 ≈ 1.333 — note the lower bound equals the empirical γ!). These are infinite-lattice statements proved by local/eigenvalue decompositions — the transplant to arbitrary min-degree-5 disks is the research gap, not the constant.\n\n**Assessment of the transfer route for M2 proper:** the transfer matrix in k applies verbatim only to *layered* (annular, Birkhoff-style) interiors, giving a ≤ c(r)·λ(r)^(#layers) with λ(r) ≈ W(4)^r. A general configuration has no canonical layer structure, so this route alone doesn't prove the Cap — but see §5: the data says the extremal configurations are wheel-like (layered), so \"transfer bound + extremality-of-layered structure theorem\" is a genuine path to the sharp constant.\n\n## 4. Route 3 — Whitney/Tutte and modern counting: the upper-bound literature is essentially empty (good news)\n\n- Lower/\"exponentially many\" results, none bearing on upper caps but defining the field's state ([FV] http://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all:%22exponentially+many%22+AND+all:%22colorings%22+AND+all:%22planar%22): Thomassen's exponentially-many-5-colorings line, now Langhede–Thomassen ≥ 2^(n/9) Z5-colorings (arXiv:2011.12163); Asadi–Dvořák–Postle–Thomas 2^√(n/362) 3-colorings triangle-free (1007.1430); Kelly–Postle 4-list-colorings on surfaces (1602.04717); and notably **Dvořák–Postle's upper-bound construction** 64^(n^0.731) killing the exponential 3-coloring conjecture (2108.12669) — the one modern precedent for *upper*-bounding coloring counts of a planar family, via recursive gadget substitution; their bootstrapping trick is reusable for showing your γ cannot be pushed below the true growth.\n- **Maximizing #colorings with given n, m**: Loh–Pikhurko–Sudakov, \"Maximizing the number of q-colorings\" [FV] https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.2625 — extremal graphs (complete bipartite minus a star) are wildly non-planar; the planar/triangulation-constrained version of the Linial–Wilf problem is **open**, and the q=4 disk-with-min-degree-5 version even more so.\n- **Tomescu's classical maxima** [KB, Semantic Scholar 429'd]: over 2-connected n-vertex graphs, max P(G,q) = (q−1)^n + (−1)^n(q−1), attained by the cycle — at q=4 that is 3^n + 3, *strictly worse* than the shelling bound 24·2^(n−3) for triangulations. Confirms: **no published bound beats §2 for this class; the Cap theorem is new territory.**\n\n## 5. Each closing step adds a chord constraint; \"generically\" that cuts colorings by 3/4 (→ γ = 1.5), but a closing chord can be an *implied* constraint (factor 1), so no per-step bound exists — needs an amortized/entropy argument exploiting interior degree ≥ 5 (a degree-5 interior vertex's link is an odd cycle, which forces ≥3 colors on the link and kills the 2-colorable-link colorings that make chords redundant). GAP: their argument uses lattice regularity; min-degree-5 disks are irregular. Medium risk, best rigorous constant available.\n3. **Layered extremality + transfer matrix (sharp γ = 4/3?).** Prove max_a(r,k) is attained by wheel-like/layered configurations (data: the wheel binds every fitted envelope), then compute the layer operator's norm exactly via the FK/TL transfer matrices of Jacobsen–Salas–Sokal [FV].
